rv.q: Redmond is compelling in Roxana Silbert's carefully controlled production.
She’s magnificent, and this Happy Days makes absurdism seem not only approachable but essential.
Winnie is a demanding part, and Redmond does an impressive job, even if there is more to be mined from it than she manages here.

This is the pinnacle production of Happy Days , a triumph of tragicomedic endurance, and the strongest production (thus far) of Alan Cumming ’s inaugural season at the theatre, and a deservedly celebrated performance from one of Scotland’s best; brava to Redmond.
The star-led new production in the Studio at Pitlochry Festival Theatre is a thoroughly compelling and touching exploration of these themes, wonderfully staged and beautifully acted.
Redmond is perfectly cast and un-knockdownable in every sense of the word.

cn.t: Critics praise this compelling production of Beckett's existential masterpiece, with Siobhan Redmond delivering a heroic performance as the eternally optimistic Winnie. The staging resonates powerfully with contemporary climate anxieties.
